title: Big Number Hunt
text: Find 5 numbers over 10,000 in real life (a car's odometer, a house price, a town's population). Write each one and the value of its biggest digit.

title: Cheque Writer
text: With an adult, look at a sample cheque or a form that asks for an amount in words. Write 3 amounts over $1,000 in words with no spelling mistakes.

title: Price Ranking
text: Find 5 used vehicles or houses for sale online with an adult. Order them from least to greatest price. Which would you choose, and why?

title: Grocery Estimator
text: Go shopping with an adult. Round each item to the nearest dollar and keep a running estimate in your head. How close were you to the real total?

title: Calculator Coach
text: Make 5 calculator problems with one mistake hidden in each. Trade with a classmate and see who finds all the mistakes by estimating.

title: Integer Spotter
text: Find 5 places integers show up in your life this week (weather app, a bank balance, sports stats, an elevator with basement floors). Write each one as an integer.

title: Weather Week
text: Record the low temperature in your town for 7 days. Put the temperatures in order on a number line and circle the coldest day.

title: Morning to Afternoon
text: For 5 days, record the temperature before school and after school. Calculate how much it rose or fell each day.

title: Chinook Watch
text: Find a news story or weather record about a big Alberta chinook. How many degrees did the temperature change, and how fast?

title: Oven Translator
text: Find 2 recipes at home or online that use °F. Use the chart to give the oven temperature in °C, then help an adult bake one of them.

title: Coin Count
text: Empty a jar or wallet of coins with an adult. Count the total and write it as a decimal. Bonus: show it with the fewest coins possible.

title: Gas Price Check
text: Record the price per litre at 3 gas stations (or on an app). Order them from cheapest to most expensive.

title: Receipt Audit
text: Ask an adult for a grocery receipt. Add up 5 items yourself and check them against the receipt.

title: Store Cashier
text: Work a shift as the class store cashier (or practise at home with play money). Make change correctly for 5 customers in a row.

title: Party Planner
text: Plan snacks for a class celebration with a $40 budget. List the items, quantities and prices, and show the total and cost per student.

title: Pack Planner
text: Find 2 things at the grocery store that come in different pack sizes (hot dogs and buns, cups and plates). Figure out the smallest number of packs for no leftovers.

title: Prime Hunter
text: Make a hundreds chart and cross out multiples of 2, 3, 5 and 7 (but not those numbers themselves). Circle what's left: those are the primes up to 100.

title: Recipe Remix
text: Find a recipe with at least 3 fractions in it. Rewrite each amount as an equivalent fraction, then cut the recipe in half.

title: Wrench Sorter
text: Find a set of wrenches or drill bits marked in inches (3/8, 1/2, 5/16…). Put them in order from smallest to largest using fractions. Ask an adult to check.

title: Kitchen Fractions
text: Help cook or bake something at home. Add up all the cups (or teaspoons) of ingredients using fractions. Show your work.

title: Time Audit
text: Track how you spend one full day in hours and minutes (sleep, school, screens, chores). Make a chart. Does it add up to 24 hours?

title: Schedule Switch
text: Rewrite your weekly class schedule (or a bus schedule) in 24-hour time.

title: Workout Timer
text: Time 5 activities in seconds (a lap, a set of push-ups, tying shoes). Convert each one to minutes as a decimal.

title: Shift Tracker
text: Ask an adult who works shifts to show you a schedule or timecard (no pay amounts needed). Calculate their total hours for one week.

title: Summer Job Budget
text: Imagine a summer job: pick a wage and hours per week for 8 weeks. Calculate your total gross pay and plan what you'd do with it.

title: Pattern Photographer
text: Take or draw 5 pictures of patterns you find at home, outside or in town. Describe what repeats or grows in each one.

title: Saving Goal
text: Pick something you want to buy. Make a table showing how much you'd save each week and predict the week you'll reach your goal.

title: Variable Menu
text: Make a price list for a pretend food truck. Write an expression for the cost of buying any number of each item, like 5b for b burgers at $5.

title: Balance Builder
text: Build a simple balance with a ruler and cups, or draw one. Show 3 equations with real objects and explain how you kept each one balanced.

title: Mystery Number Cards
text: Make 5 "mystery number" cards with real-life equations (like 12n = 60 for movie tickets). Trade with a classmate and solve each other's.

title: Measure Up
text: Measure 5 things at home in both inches and centimetres (a door, a table, your height). Use the chart to check your measurements match.

title: Baseboard Estimate
text: Measure the perimeter of your bedroom (subtract the door width). How many metres of baseboard would you need?

title: Paint Planner
text: Measure one wall at home. Find its area, subtract any window or door, and find out how many cans of paint you'd need (check the coverage on a paint can or website).

title: String Test
text: Wrap a string around 3 round things (a can, a plate, a bucket). Measure the string and the diameter. Divide: do you get close to 3.14 every time?

title: Dream Room
text: Draw a floor plan of your dream bedroom on grid paper (1 square = 0.5 m). Label furniture with ordered pairs, and find the floor area and perimeter.

title: Scale Detective
text: Use a kitchen or bathroom scale to weigh 5 things at home. Record each in grams or kilograms AND pounds.

title: Pour Test
text: Use a measuring cup to find how much your favourite mug, a water bottle and a bowl hold. Record each in mL and L.

title: Box Check
text: Measure a small box or container in cm, calculate its volume, then fill it with water using a measuring cup. How close were you?

title: Shape Scavenger Hunt
text: Find and photograph a real example of each 3-D object at home or school. Label the faces, edges and vertices on one of them.

title: Package Designer
text: Design and build a gift box from a net you draw yourself. Measure it and find its volume in cm³.

title: Class Survey
text: Survey the class about one question (favourite store item, how they get to school). Record the results in a tally chart.

title: Graph in the News
text: Find a graph in a news story, sports website or flyer. Write the title, what each axis shows, and one thing the graph tells you.

title: Spreadsheet Chart
text: Put your class survey results into a spreadsheet (Google Sheets or Excel) and make a bar graph with a title and labels.

title: Store Advisor
text: Look at a month of Avalanche HQ sales with your teacher. Write a short report with one conclusion and one prediction, and suggest a change to the store.

title: Probability Lab
text: Do a real experiment at home: flip a coin 50 times or roll a die 60 times. Record the results in a table and graph, and compare them to what you expected.

title: Million Hunt
text: Find 3 real numbers in the millions in the news, on a sports contract or on a real estate site. Write each one in numerals and in words.

title: Zero Count
text: Teach a Grade 8 classmate the "count the zeros" trick for powers of 10. Have them write 3 numbers in expanded form and check their work.

title: Space Numbers
text: Look up 3 distances in space (Earth to Moon, Earth to Mars, Earth to Sun). Write each in standard form and in scientific notation.

title: Receipt Rounder
text: Collect a grocery receipt or flyer. Round 5 prices to the nearest dollar and add them up. How close is your estimate to the real total?

title: Estimate First
text: For one week, estimate the total before you pay for anything (snacks, groceries with family, a game). Record your estimate and the real total.

title: Money Diary
text: For one week, record every time money comes in or goes out for you (or pretend with a $100 budget). Write each as a positive or negative integer.

title: Weather Watch
text: Check the overnight low for 5 Canadian cities on a weather app. Put them in order from coldest to warmest.

title: Statement Builder
text: Make a pretend bank statement for one month with at least 6 deposits and withdrawals. Have a classmate check your running balance.

title: Debt Detective
text: Ask a family member or look online: what does your bank charge for an overdraft or NSF fee? Write a short tip sheet for a friend on how to avoid it.

title: Chinook Tracker
text: Teach a Grade 8 classmate how to find the change in temperature across zero. Use real high and low temperatures from this week.

title: Flyer Math
text: Use a grocery flyer to pick 4 items sold by weight. Choose an amount for each and calculate what you'd pay. Round to the cent.

title: Fair Share
text: Plan a pizza party for your class: find the real price of the pizzas and drinks, then work out what each person would pay.

title: Catch the Mistake
text: Write 5 decimal problems with answers. Make 2 of them wrong on purpose. Trade with a classmate and see if they can catch the mistakes by estimating.

title: Average Me
text: Track something about yourself for 7 days (hours of sleep, minutes on your phone, steps). Find your mean and decide if it surprised you.

title: Spreadsheet Coach
text: Set up a Google Sheet that tracks a Grade 8 classmate's AvCash for 5 weeks. Show them how =SUM and =AVERAGE work.

title: Shift Schedules
text: Two friends work part-time. One works every 3rd day and one every 4th day. Mark a one-month calendar to show the days they both work. Explain how the LCM helps you predict those days.

title: Care Packages
text: Plan care packages for a food bank or shelter using real amounts of 2 or 3 items. Use the GCF to find the most identical packages you can make.

title: Tree Challenge
text: Make factor trees for 60 two different ways (start with 6 × 10, then 4 × 15). Do you get the same primes? Show a classmate why.

title: Measure It
text: Use a tape measure to find the length and width of 3 things at home to the nearest 1/4 inch. Add the length and width of each as mixed numbers.

title: Recipe Remix
text: Find a recipe that uses at least 3 different fractions. Add up all the dry ingredients in cups using a common denominator.

title: Time Card
text: Make a time card for a week of your life: school, sports, homework, screen time. Add up each category in hours and minutes.

title: Job Shopping
text: Find 3 real part-time job postings for teens in your area. Calculate what each would pay for 15 hours a week and for a whole summer (10 weeks).

title: Know Your Rights
text: Visit Alberta's employment standards website and find 3 rules that protect young workers (breaks, hours, overtime). Make a poster for the class.

title: Career Pay Check
text: Pick 2 careers you're interested in on ALIS. Find out how each is usually paid (wage, salary, commission or tips) and the typical pay.

title: Stub Decoder
text: Ask a family member if you can look at an old pay stub (cover the private parts). Find the gross pay, each deduction and the net pay. What percent of the gross was taken off?

title: Pattern Predictor
text: Find a real pattern in your life (a bus schedule, bowling scores, savings, a growing plant). Make a table and predict the next 5 steps. Check one prediction later.

title: Plan Comparison
text: Find 2 real phone or streaming plans. Write a rule for each and figure out which is cheaper for how you actually use it.

title: Equation Coach
text: Help a Grade 8 classmate solve 3 one-step equations, then show them how a two-step equation is just one more step. Make up the problems from real prices.

title: Graph It
text: Pick a rule from Lesson 2 (like a taxi or phone plan). Make a table of values with 6 rows and graph it on grid paper or in Google Sheets.

title: Best Deal Graph
text: Compare 2 real options with different starting fees (bowling alleys, rental places, ride shares). Graph both and find where they cross. Share your advice with a family member.

title: Garden Planner
text: You have 20 m of fence. Draw 4 different rectangular gardens on grid paper and find each area. Which one would you build, and why?

title: Roof Finder
text: Find a triangle shape on a building near you (a roof, a sign, a bridge). Estimate or measure its base and height and find its area.

title: Angle Hunt
text: Photograph one example of each kind of angle at home or school. Estimate each one, then measure it with a protractor.

title: Truss Builder
text: Build a triangle truss out of straws or popsicle sticks. Measure its angles with a protractor and check that they add to 180°.

title: Treasure Map
text: Draw a map of your neighbourhood or school with a scale. Write step-by-step directions (like "go 3 squares left, 2 up") to a hidden "treasure" and have a classmate follow them.

title: Trunk Detective
text: Wrap a measuring tape around 3 trees or poles. Use the circumference to work out each diameter. Which is the widest?

title: Kitchen Converter
text: Find 5 packages at home that show both metric and imperial (cans, cereal boxes, milk jugs). Check one conversion on each with the chart.

title: Gift Wrapper
text: Pick a real box at home. Measure it, find its surface area, then cut wrapping paper (or newspaper) to cover it. How much extra did you need for overlap?

title: Skeleton Crew
text: Build skeletons of 3 different 3-D objects with toothpicks and modelling clay (or straws and tape). Count the edges and vertices of each and sketch them.

title: Logo Lab
text: Design a logo for Avalanche HQ or a pretend business using at least 2 transformations. Label each flip, slide or turn and show any lines of symmetry.

title: Graph in the Wild
text: Find a graph in the news, a sports site or an app. Write its title, what each axis shows, and one conclusion you can make from it.

title: Class Survey
text: Survey at least 15 people with one question (favourite snack for the store, how they get to school). Make a frequency table and choose the best graph to show the results.

title: Stat Line
text: Pick a sports team or player. Collect their points (or goals) for 7 games and find the range, median and mean. Which number best describes how they're doing?

title: Data Detective
text: Put your Class Survey data into Google Sheets. Use =MAX, =MIN, =AVERAGE and =MEDIAN, make a chart, and write 2 conclusions the data supports.

title: Run the Odds
text: With a Grade 8 partner, roll a real die 60 times and record the results. Compare your results with the simulator. How close did each number get to 1 out of 6?

title: Where Does My Water Come From?
text: Find out where your town or farm gets its water (a river, a lake, a well). Draw a map from the source to your tap.

title: Water Tester
text: With your teacher's kit or test strips, test tap water, rain or snowmelt, and pond or slough water. Compare the pH and hardness in a chart.

lessonTitle: The water cycle and the land
title: Water Cycle in a Bag
text: Put a little water in a sealed zip bag, tape it to a sunny window and watch it for a week. Draw and label each step of the water cycle you see.

title: Pond Life
text: Look up (or visit with an adult) 3 animals that live in an Alberta pond, slough or lake. Draw each one and label one adaptation that helps it survive.

title: Water Saver
text: Track how much water your household uses in one day (showers, dishes, laundry). Make a plan with 3 ways your family could save water, and try one for a week.

title: Then and Now
text: Interview a grandparent or older neighbour about a machine they used growing up (a wringer washer, a hand pump, a crank phone). Compare it with what we use now.

title: Machine Hunt
text: Find all six simple machines at home or in the school shop. Photograph or sketch each one and label it.

title: Lever Lab
text: Build a lever with a ruler and a pencil as the fulcrum. Lift a stack of coins with coins on the other end. Move the fulcrum and record how many coins it takes each time.

title: Bike Tech
text: Look at a bike (yours or a shop's). Count the teeth on the front and back gears. Explain which combination is best for hills and which is best for speed.

title: Build and Test
text: Design and build a machine that lifts a small load (a pulley, crane or catapult) from recycled materials. Test it, then rate it on function, safety and efficiency.

title: Food Finders
text: Pick 4 Alberta animals or plants. Make a chart showing how each one gets food, water and oxygen.

title: Cell Model
text: Build a model of a plant or animal cell with food or craft supplies. Label every part and explain what it does.

title: Workplace Comparison
text: Compare your body's levels to a business: cells are workers, tissues are teams, organs are departments. Make a poster that shows the comparison.

title: Heart Rate Lab
text: Take your pulse for 15 seconds and multiply by 4. Do it resting, after walking and after 1 minute of jumping jacks. Graph your results.

title: Healthy Habit Challenge
text: Pick one habit that helps a body system (more water, 30 minutes of activity, earlier bedtime). Track it for 2 weeks and report how you felt.

title: Lighting Then and Now
text: Ask an older relative how homes were lit when they were young. Count the light sources in your home now and sort them as incandescent, fluorescent or LED.

title: Periscope Builder
text: Build a periscope from a milk carton and two small mirrors. Use it to see over a table. Draw the path the light takes.

title: Material Sort
text: Test 10 materials at home with a flashlight. Sort them as transparent, translucent or opaque in a chart.

title: Water Lens
text: Put a drop of water on clear plastic wrap over newspaper print. What happens to the letters? Explain what kind of lens the drop makes.

title: Eye Exam Explainer
text: Find out what happens at an eye exam (ask an optometrist, a family member or look it up). Make a short guide for a classmate who has never had one.

title: Plate Planner
text: Plan 3 meals for one day that follow Canada's Food Guide. Include at least one traditional or cultural food that matters to you or your family.

title: Fish Advisory
text: Look up Alberta's fish consumption advice for a lake near you. Make a simple poster for anglers explaining why it exists.

title: Cabbage Indicator
text: With an adult, make red cabbage juice indicator. Test 6 kitchen liquids (vinegar, baking soda water, milk, lemon juice, soap, tap water) and rank them by pH.

title: Quality Report
text: Check today's AQHI for your area and find your town's latest drinking water report online. Write a short "quality report" for your class.

title: Eco-Station Guide
text: Find where your community takes household hazardous waste. Make a one-page guide for your family listing what goes there and when it's open.

title: Lemon Battery
text: With an adult, make a wet cell from a lemon (or potato), a copper coin and a galvanized nail. Connect a few in a row and try to light a small LED.

title: Safety Sweep
text: Do an electrical safety check at home with an adult: overloaded power bars, frayed cords, outlets near water. Write down 3 things that are safe and 1 thing to fix.

title: Circuit Builder
text: Use a circuit kit or the PhET simulation to build a series circuit and a parallel circuit with 2 bulbs each. Remove one bulb from each and record what happens.

title: Energy Detective
text: Find the wattage label on 5 devices at home. Estimate how many hours a day each runs and calculate the daily kWh. Which one costs the most? Suggest a way to cut it.

title: Grid Watch
text: Look up the Alberta Electric System Operator's (AESO) current supply mix. Make a bar graph of how much power comes from each source right now and compare it with another day.

title: Diversity Count
text: In a 1 m × 1 m square of lawn, field or garden, count how many different kinds of plants and bugs you can find. Compare with a classmate's square.

title: Food Web
text: Make a food web for an Alberta habitat (prairie, boreal forest, wetland) with at least 8 species. Circle one species and explain what would happen if it disappeared.

title: Grow a Clone
text: Grow a new plant from a cutting (a spider plant, a pothos or a potato with eyes). Track it for 3 weeks. Explain why it's a clone of the parent.

title: Trait Survey
text: Survey 10 people for 3 inherited traits (attached earlobes, can roll tongue, dimples). Make a bar graph. Bonus: help a Grade 8 classmate graph theirs.

title: Species Spotlight
text: Pick an Alberta species at risk. Make a poster or short video: where it lives, why it's at risk and one thing people can do to help. Share it with a younger class.

title: Sky Stories
text: Learn one star story or constellation from a First Nations, Métis or Inuit source, and one from another culture. Compare what each says about the sky.

title: Scale Model
text: Make a scale model of planet distances in a hallway or field using toilet paper squares or steps. Teach a Grade 8 class what you learned.

title: Moon Journal
text: Sketch the Moon every clear night for 2 weeks and note the date. Label the phases and predict what it will look like next week.

title: Mission Planner
text: Plan the supplies for a 6-month space mission for 4 people: air, water, food, exercise and waste. Explain how you'd recycle as much as possible.

title: Space Debate
text: Should countries be allowed to mine the Moon? Write or record a 1-minute argument for one side, then list the best point the other side would make.

title: Identity Map
text: Make your own identity map with at least 6 branches. Add a photo, drawing or object for each one.

title: Story Swap
text: Write a narrative paragraph about a moment that changed you. Read it to a family member and ask them to tell you a story from their life in return.

title: Family Story
text: Ask an older family member or community member to tell you a story they were told when they were young. Retell it to the class (with their permission) and explain what it teaches.

title: Goal Tracker
text: Set one SMART reading or writing goal. Track it for 4 weeks and write 3 sentences about how it went.

title: Kindness Crew
text: Plan and run a small act that helps someone new feel welcome at school (a lunch invite, a welcome card, showing them around). Write about how it went.

title: Translator
text: Collect 5 texts or social posts (no names!) and rewrite each one in formal language, as if it were going to a boss.

title: Inbox Helper
text: Write a real, polite email to a teacher, coach or club leader asking a question you actually have. Show it to your teacher before you send it.

title: Gratitude Letter
text: Write a real thank-you letter to someone who helped you or the class this year (a bus driver, custodian, coach or family member) and deliver it.

title: Form Pro
text: Fill out a practice job application from your teacher with zero mistakes. Use made-up information for anything private.

title: Recipe Run
text: Follow a written recipe at home from start to finish with no help, then teach a family member how to make it using only your own words.

title: Editor on Duty
text: Be the class editor for a week: proofread 3 classmates' emails or letters and help them fix every mistake before they hand them in.

title: Movie Mountain
text: Pick your favourite movie or show episode and draw its plot mountain with all six parts labelled.

title: Then and Now
text: Choose a character from a book, show or game who changes. Make a two-column chart: what they were like at the start and at the end, with proof for each.

title: Hook Challenge
text: Write 3 different opening sentences for the same story: one with a question, one with action, one with a strange detail. Ask 3 people which one makes them want to keep reading.

title: Mood Swap
text: Take a photo of one place at home or school. Write two short descriptions of it: one cozy, one creepy.

title: Readers Theatre
text: With 2–4 classmates, turn a short story or fable into a 2-minute script. Rehearse and perform it for another class or record it.

title: Scavenger Scan
text: Find 5 everyday texts at home (a recipe, a label, a flyer, a schedule, a menu). Write one question for each and time how fast a family member can find the answer.

title: Fact Hunt
text: Find a product review or a sports article. Highlight facts in one colour and opinions in another. Which was there more of?

title: Fact Checker
text: Find one surprising claim online. Check it with 2 trusted sources and report whether it's true, false or misleading.

title: News Compare
text: Follow one local news story on two different media (a radio station and a website, for example). Write what each one included and left out.

title: Ad Detective
text: Collect 5 ads (flyers, video ads, social posts). Name the technique each one uses and rate how well it worked on you.

title: Change Maker
text: Pick a real change you want at home, school or in your town. Write who the audience is and what you want them to do.

title: Letter of Change
text: Write a persuasive paragraph or letter about your Change Maker topic and send it to the real person who can make it happen (with your teacher's help).

title: Editing Buddy
text: Trade persuasive paragraphs with a classmate. Give 2 compliments, 1 revising idea and check their CUPS.

title: PSA Poster
text: Design a PSA poster or 30-second video for a real issue at your school or in your community. Ask to display or share it.

title: Pitch It
text: Present your PSA to a younger class, a family member or the school announcements. Ask for one piece of feedback.

title: Career Pick
text: Choose 3 careers you're curious about. Write 5W + H questions for the one you'll research first.

title: ALIS Explorer
text: Find your career on ALIS. Record 3 duties, the education needed, the wage range and one reading or writing task the job uses.

title: Interview Notes
text: Interview someone about their job (5 questions). Take point-form notes and turn them into a short profile.

title: Habit Tracker
text: Pick 2 worker habits. Track them every school day for 2 weeks and ask a teacher or coach to sign off when they notice.

title: Portfolio Launch
text: Set up a Google Drive folder or binder for your portfolio with at least 5 items. Show it to a family member and explain each piece.

title: Choice Map
text: Pick a character from a book, show or game. Map 3 big choices they made, the motive behind each, and what each one shows about them.

title: Theme Song
text: Choose a song or short film (school-appropriate). Write its topic, its theme in one sentence and 2 pieces of evidence.

title: Story Keeper
text: Record or write down a story from an Elder, grandparent or community member (with permission). Explain what it shows about their values and traditions.

title: Identity Essay
text: Write a three-paragraph essay about an experience that shaped who you are. Add it to your portfolio.

title: Lead the Way
text: Volunteer to lead a group task (in class, sports, a club or at home). Afterwards, rate yourself out of 5 on listening, organizing and encouraging, with a reason for each.

title: Skills Inventory
text: Interview 2 adults who know you (family, coach, teacher). Ask them for 3 skills they see in you. Add the best ones to your career portfolio.

title: Résumé Ready
text: Finish a full one-page résumé, get feedback from one adult outside school, and revise it. Add the final copy to your career portfolio.

title: Real Posting
text: Find a real job posting in your town (Job Bank or a store website). Write a cover letter for it, as if you were 16.

title: Store Memo
text: Write a real memo to the class about an Avalanche HQ change (new item, sale day, store hours) and post it in the classroom.

title: Reference Ask
text: Ask 2 adults (not family) to be your references, using a polite email or in person. Record their contact information in your portfolio.

title: Mock Interview
text: Complete a mock interview with an adult who isn't your teacher (a family friend or a local business owner). Ask them to fill out the feedback checklist.

title: Chapter Log
text: Keep a one-line summary and one question for every chapter you read. Share your favourite question with the class.

title: Arc Chart
text: Make an arc chart for the main character in your novel with a quote or event for the beginning, middle and end.

title: Shot Spotter
text: Watch a 3-minute movie trailer. List 5 shots and explain what each camera angle, lighting or sound choice makes you feel.

title: Double Feature
text: Pick a book and movie pair you know (or a graphic novel and its show). Make a Venn diagram and decide which version is better, with 3 reasons.

title: Critic's Corner
text: Write a review of the novel or film and post it (with your teacher's help) on the school library page or in a class "Critic's Corner" binder.

title: Headline Flip
text: Find a news headline. Rewrite it twice: once biased for, once biased against. Then write the most neutral version.

title: CRAAP Test
text: Pick 2 websites on the same topic. Score each out of 5 for every part of the CRAAP test and decide which one to trust.

title: Crop It
text: Take one photo and crop it 2 ways to tell 2 different stories. Write a caption for each.

title: Media Breakdown
text: Analyze one ad, music video or influencer post using the 5 questions. Present your breakdown to a Grade 8 group.

title: Footprint Check
text: With a family member, search your name online and check your privacy settings on one app. Write 3 changes you made or will make.

title: Both Sides
text: Choose an issue you care about. Make a T-chart with 4 reasons for each side, then write your thesis.

title: Evidence Bank
text: Find 2 pieces of evidence for each of your 3 reasons. Record the source for each.

title: Essay Draft
text: Draft your five-paragraph essay. Add it to your portfolio once it's final.

title: Read It Aloud
text: Read your essay out loud to someone. Fix every spot where you stumble or they look confused.

title: PSA Campaign
text: Team up with a Grade 8 group to launch a PSA campaign at school: posters, an announcement and a short video on the same issue.

title: Growth Proof
text: Find your first and best piece of writing from this year. Write what improved and how you know.

title: Pathway Visit
text: Visit (or look up) your future high school's course guide. Find 3 courses or programs that connect to a career you're interested in.

title: Research Reflection
text: Write a 5-sentence reflection on your career research: what worked, what didn't and one change for next time.

title: My Plan
text: Write your transition plan and share it with a parent or guardian. Ask them to add one support or idea.

title: Showcase Night
text: Present your portfolio at a student-led conference or a class showcase. Invite a family member or a mentor.

title: Worldview Shield
text: Design a shield with 4 sections: family, beliefs, place and experiences. Fill each with words or pictures that shape your worldview.

title: Three Views
text: Pick a current issue in your community. Interview or research 3 people with different perspectives on it and summarize each.

title: Family Artifact
text: Bring in (or photograph) an old object or photo from your family. Explain what it tells us about the past and who made it.

title: My Timeline
text: Make a timeline of your life (or your family's history) with at least 8 events. Mark each decade.

title: Land Connection
text: Find out whose traditional territory your school is on (Treaty 6, 7 or 8, or Métis homeland). Learn one teaching or place name from that Nation and share it.

title: My Worldview Map
text: Make a poster or slide showing 3 beliefs, 3 values and 3 things you know that shape how you see the world, and where each one came from.

title: Map Maker
text: Draw a labelled map of Japan showing the 4 main islands, Tokyo (once called Edo), Nagasaki and the Pacific Ocean. Add a key.

title: Pros and Cons Debate
text: Prepare 3 reasons FOR and 3 reasons AGAINST Japan's isolation. Lead a 5-minute class debate.

title: Two Points of View
text: Write two short diary entries about the day the black ships arrived: one from a Japanese fisher and one from an American sailor.

title: Then and Now
text: Interview an adult about the biggest change they've seen in their lifetime (phones, jobs, technology). What did people gain, and what did they lose? Compare it to the Meiji era.

lessonTitle: Change and tradition here at home
title: Local Voices
text: With your teacher's help, find out which First Nations or Métis communities are near your school and one way they keep their language or traditions strong today. Share what you learned respectfully with the class.

title: Modern Patron
text: Who are today's "patrons" of art, music or sport (sponsors, grants, crowdfunding)? Find one example and explain how it works.

title: Renaissance Me
text: List 5 different skills you have or want to build (art, sport, tech, cooking, music). Make a "Renaissance résumé" for yourself.

title: Then and Now Ideas
text: Compare the printing press to the internet or social media. Make a chart showing 3 ways they're similar and 3 ways they're different.

title: Trade Route Map
text: Draw a map of one Renaissance trade or exploration route. Label what was traded and what dangers sailors faced.

title: Renaissance Today
text: Find 3 things in your life (a school subject, an invention, a value) with roots in the Renaissance. Make a poster connecting then and now.

title: City Planner
text: Draw or build a model of Tenochtitlan with its causeways, temple and chinampas. Label how each part met people's needs.

title: Motive Ranking
text: Rank gold, God and glory for Spain from most to least important. Defend your ranking in a paragraph or a short recording.

title: Cause Web
text: Make a cause-and-effect web showing why Tenochtitlan fell. Rank the causes and explain your top one.

title: Word Detective
text: Find 5 words in English that come from Nahuatl or another Indigenous language of the Americas. Make a mini-dictionary.

title: Contact Debate
text: With a partner, argue which society faced the bigger challenge at contact: the Aztecs or Japan. Use at least 3 facts each.

title: Contact Comic
text: Make a 3-panel comic: one panel each for Japan, the Renaissance and the Aztecs, showing how each met another worldview.

title: Language Learner
text: Learn 10 words in Cree, Blackfoot, Dene, Michif or another language spoken in Alberta. Teach them to someone at home.

title: Media Check
text: Watch a show, movie or ad that includes a culture different from yours. Was it fair and accurate? Who made it? Write a short review.

title: Issue Watch
text: Follow a current issue in the news for 2 weeks. Complete all 4 steps of the issue-analysis model.

title: Action Project
text: With a small group, plan and carry out one action on an issue (a food drive, a cultural celebration, an awareness poster campaign). Report on what you did and what changed.

title: Rights in Real Life
text: Find a news story where someone's Charter right was involved. Explain which right and what happened.

title: Rights Sort
text: Make a two-column chart of 6 individual and 4 collective rights, with a real example of each.

title: Francophone Alberta
text: Find one Francophone community, school or festival in Alberta. Share 3 facts about it and one French phrase you learned.

title: Treaty Territory
text: Find out which treaty area your school is in and which Nations signed it. Make a map with the date and one promise from the treaty.

title: Journey Story
text: Interview someone who immigrated to Canada (or research a newcomer's story). What brought them here? What challenges did they face?

title: Price Tracker
text: Track the price of one thing (gas, eggs, a game) for 3 weeks. Graph it and explain any change using supply and demand.

title: Debate Prep
text: Write a one-minute speech arguing for MORE government involvement in one area (like daycare or housing), then a one-minute speech arguing for LESS. Which was easier to argue, and why?

lessonTitle: Canada and the U.S.: trading partners
title: Label Hunt
text: Check 10 products at home and record where each was made. How many came from the U.S.? Make a chart and bring it to class.

title: Resource Career Card
text: Use ALIS to research one Alberta career that depends on a natural resource. Make a card showing what they do, the training needed and the average pay.

title: Town Hall
text: Pick a real Alberta resource issue in the news. Write a short letter to your MLA explaining your position, using one fact for each side. Show your teacher before sending.

title: Union Interview
text: Interview an adult who is in a union or professional association. Ask what it does for them and one thing they'd change. Share both sides with the class.

title: Who's Who
text: Find out who your MP, MLA, mayor or reeve, and a Supreme Court justice are. Make a "who's who" chart for your family.

title: Bill Tracker
text: Find a real bill being debated in Parliament or the Alberta Legislature. Track which stage it's at and what it would change.

title: Platform Compare
text: Pick 2 parties and one issue you care about. Compare what each party's website says about it.

title: Court Visit
text: Visit a courthouse open session (with an adult), watch a mock trial video, or interview a lawyer or police officer about their job. Write 3 things that surprised you.

title: Write Your Rep
text: Write a respectful email or letter to your MP or MLA about an issue you care about. Share any reply you get.

title: Good Life Survey
text: Ask 5 people of different ages what makes a good life. Sort their answers into standard of living and quality of life.

title: Buy Nothing Day
text: Go 3 days without buying anything you don't need. Track every time an ad tempted you, and how you felt.

title: Tax Trail
text: Pick one public service you used this week (a road, a hospital, a park). Find out which level of government pays for it.

title: Program Profile
text: Choose one social program. Find out who it helps, how it's paid for, and one argument for and against expanding it.

title: Platform Detective
text: Choose one issue (housing, health care, jobs). Compare what 2 or 3 parties' platforms say about it, using their own websites. Stay neutral and just report.

title: Resource Map
text: Map 3 resource industries near where you live. For each, list one benefit and one concern for your community.

title: Role Play Hearing
text: Hold a mock public hearing on an Alberta issue. Each person plays one stakeholder and argues their interests. Then vote as "council."

title: Trend Spotter
text: Find one graph about Alberta's energy, water or wildlife from a government or StatCan site. Describe the trend and one possible cause.

title: Two Sides Media
text: Find two articles or videos with different views on the same environmental issue. Highlight facts and opinions in each.

title: Future Forum
text: Present your position on an Alberta environmental issue in a short speech, poster or video. Invite a community member or local councillor to hear it.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Job Then and Now
text: Interview an adult about a job they had that has changed (or disappeared) because of technology. What new skills did they need?

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Skill Ranking
text: List 8 skills you have. Rank them from strongest to weakest and give a real example for your top 3.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Learn Something New
text: Learn a new skill in 2 weeks (a coding basic, a recipe, a tool, a language phrase set). Show what you learned and how it adds to your human capital.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Role Model Profile
text: Find someone from a group that's under-represented in their career (in your community or online). Make a profile of their path and the barriers they overcame.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Milestone Map
text: Draw a career path map with one long-term goal and at least 4 milestones. Add one backup route.

title: Offer Detective
text: Ask an adult you trust what their first job offer included. Fill out a chart with the pay, hours, duties and extras.

title: Dream Job Math
text: Look up the hourly wage for a job you'd like on ALIS. Calculate the weekly and yearly pay for full-time work.

title: Benefits Value
text: With an adult's help, find out what one benefit costs without insurance (an eye exam and glasses, or a dental cleaning). That's how much a benefit can be worth!

title: My Top 3
text: Rank the 6 non-salary factors from most to least important to you, and explain your top 3 to a family member. Did their list match yours?

title: Offer Showdown
text: Find 2 real job postings in your area for teens or students. Make a comparison chart and choose one. Explain your choice to the class.

title: Career Conversation
text: Have a 10-minute conversation with an adult about their career using at least 3 of the starters. Write down the 3 most useful things you learned.

title: First Paycheque
text: Ask a family member how they felt about their first paycheque. Was it more or less than they expected?

title: Bracket Myth Buster
text: Many people think a raise into a higher bracket means you take home less. Make a short explainer (poster or video) showing why that's not true.

title: Fair Tax Debate
text: Which system is fairest? Write your opinion with 2 reasons, then write the best argument from someone who disagrees.

title: Tax Spotter
text: For one day, list every public service you use (bus, school, streetlights, library). Estimate what your day would cost if you paid for each yourself.

title: Safety Poster
text: Make a poster for teen workers showing the 3 safety rights, with a real example of each.

title: Cost Detective
text: With a family member, list 10 household costs. Sort them into fixed and variable, and circle the one that would be easiest to lower.

title: Goal Budget
text: Pick something you want to buy. Make a real or pretend monthly budget that reaches the goal, then find one variable cost to cut to get there sooner.

title: Bank Shopper
text: Find the interest rate on 2 real savings accounts for youth. Calculate the simple interest on $500 for one year at each.

title: Time Machine
text: Use an online compound interest calculator. Compare saving $50 a month starting at age 14 vs. age 30, both until age 60 at 5%. Share the difference.

title: AvCash Investor
text: Track your Avalanche HQ investment for 4 weeks. Calculate your return as a percent each week and explain your choice.

title: Program Lookup
text: Find one program at NAIT, SAIT, Olds College, a university or a trade school. Record the admission requirements and length.

title: Dream vs Data
text: Pick a dream career. Find its Alberta wage and outlook on ALIS. Write whether the data matches your expectations.

title: Scholarship Hunt
text: Find 3 scholarships or bursaries for Alberta high school graduates (try alis.alberta.ca or a local business). Record who qualifies and how to apply.

title: Career Chat
text: Have a 10-minute career conversation with an adult in a job you're curious about. Use the starters and send a thank-you message afterwards.

title: Course Plan
text: Draft a Grade 10–12 course plan for one pathway. Have a parent, teacher or counsellor check it and sign off.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Robot Watch
text: Find 3 examples of automation in your town (self-checkout, automated milking, online ordering). For each, list one job lost and one job created.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Industry Sort
text: Use ALIS or Job Bank to sort 6 Alberta industries into growing, stable or declining. Back up each with one piece of data.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Source Check
text: Find one career claim online and check it against ALIS or Job Bank. Was it accurate?

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Try It Out
text: Volunteer for at least 3 hours or run a mini-business (bake sale, lawn care, crafts). Reflect on 3 skills you used.

unitTitle: Skills, Identity & the World of Work
title: Language Asset
text: Search Job Bank for 3 postings that list a second language as required or an asset. What languages and jobs did you find?

title: Posting Match
text: Find 2 real job postings on Job Bank for jobs a 15–16-year-old could do. Highlight the skills and qualifications, then list which ones you already have.

title: Brand Check
text: Write your brand statement, then ask 3 people who know you if it sounds like you. Revise it using their feedback.

title: Two Versions
text: Make 2 versions of your résumé for 2 very different jobs. Highlight what you changed and why.

title: Job Map
text: Make a map or list of 10 places within walking or bus distance of home that hire teens. Note how each one hires: online, in person, or through people you know.

title: Digital Clean-Up
text: Search your name online with an adult, set your accounts to private, and remove anything you wouldn't want an employer to see. Write a short reflection on what you found.

title: Panel Practice
text: Do a mock interview with the Grade 8 panel, then interview a Grade 8 student about their goals so they can practise answering too.

lessonTitle: The T4 and the tax return
title: Mock Return
text: Use a sample T4 and the CRA's free learning tools to walk through a simple tax return. Did the sample person get a refund or owe money?

title: Credit Finder
text: Research 3 tax credits a young person or student could use. Explain each one in plain language for a classmate.

title: Account Advisor
text: Write advice for two people: a 19-year-old saving for a car and a 45-year-old saving for retirement. Which account fits each, and why?

title: Gig Math
text: A delivery driver earns $500 in a week from an app. Research what costs and taxes they're responsible for, and estimate what they really keep.

title: Rights Quick Guide
text: Make a one-page "know your rights" guide for a teen starting their first job in Alberta.

title: Credit Offers
text: Collect 3 credit offers from ads, mail or websites (store cards, BNPL, loans). Find the interest rate and fees in the fine print.

title: Payoff Race
text: Use an online credit card payoff calculator. Compare paying the minimum vs. $100 a month on a $1,500 balance. Record the time and total interest.

title: Credit Plan
text: Write a 5-step plan to build good credit starting at 18 (for example: one card with a low limit, pay in full, on time, every month).

title: Ad Breakdown
text: Find a payday or quick-loan ad. List the tricks it uses and calculate the real cost of borrowing $500 from it.

title: Debt Plan
text: Make up a person with 3 debts. Plan their payoff with the avalanche and snowball methods. Which would you choose for them, and why?

title: True Cost Calc
text: Pick a real Alberta program. Find tuition, fees and books, estimate living costs, and add opportunity cost. Share the true cost.

title: ROI Compare
text: Compare 2 pathways (for example, a trade and a university degree). Use ALIS wages to estimate how many years each takes to "pay back" its true cost.

title: Aid Explorer
text: Visit Alberta Student Aid's website. List the types of help available and one thing you'd need to qualify.

title: Apprentice Q&A
text: Interview an apprentice, journeyperson or co-op student (or watch a Tradesecrets video). Write 3 things you learned about earning while learning.

title: Plan A + B
text: Write your post-secondary plan with a primary pathway, a backup and a rationale. Present it to a family member or counsellor and add it to your portfolio.
